title: V2 prose hard_gates have no machine evaluator
discovered_by: real end-to-end run of stage-04-requirements-planning against the consolidated-68 recipes
evidence: 340 of 340 V2 gate strings return {'error': 'no deterministic evaluator'}
observed_failure: Running one real step produced: gate-failed: ['Review evidence only; do not create design artifacts, mutate the plan, or treat contextual aesthetics as universal law.', 'Preserve conflicts, counterevidence, unknowns, source identity, and authority boundaries.'] — the model output was a correct requirements contract, but the prose gates could not be evaluated and were therefore treated as failures.
root_cause: V1 recipes use short machine-checkable gate identifiers (source-traceability, unknown-preservation, ...). V2 recipes carry human-readable hard_gates that state obligations for the model. The executor has no evaluator for the V2 form, so every V2 step fails closed at the gate layer.
impact: The consolidated-68 recipes can be loaded, topologically ordered, and executed, but no step can pass its gates. The complete flow cannot run end to end until this layer is bridged.
bounded_next_step: Compile each V2 hard_gate into a machine predicate, either by mapping to an existing evaluator id or by adding a small set of new deterministic evaluators. Keep gate evaluation deterministic; do not replace it with model self-report.
what_already_works: recipe loading, mode-aware step resolution, and hard-dependency topological ordering
candidate_path and skill_ref resolution for all 170 steps
real model invocation with per-mode document loading
artifact persistence, state files, and per-step evidence records

resolution.approach: Two-layer gate model. Blocking gates are machine-checkable ids derived from the contract's own structural properties; the original prose obligations are preserved as recorded advisory gates and handed to independent review instead of being faked as regex checks.
resolution.calibration: Evaluated against 304 real model outputs: non-execution-stated 99%, authority-named 71%, unknowns-preserved 70%, status-declared 58% (the eval prompt never asked for a status line; the executor prompt does and passes 100%), evidence-binding 46%. 36% of outputs pass every gate that applies to them. A claim-only negative control fails every gate.
evidence: tools/curation/recipe_execute.py:evaluate_gates bridges V1 and V2 gate ids

additional_fixes.conditional_steps: 127 steps are `conditional` with `default_state: skipped`; the executor now treats a stage as an opt-in menu and reports needs-input with the available menu when nothing is activated. 27 steps marked disabled-pending-current-authorization never run.
additional_fixes.step_ordering: Dependency records name capabilities while steps are keyed by mode; the resolver now maps both. Only `hard` edges order steps: `optional` means use-if-present and `feedback` is explicitly a future-pass edge, and treating either as ordering creates cycles.
additional_fixes.caller_order: An ordered activation list is honoured for steps whose prerequisites hold.
additional_fixes.composite_runner: Added execute_composite: walks stage_steps in dependency order, enforces the four handoff obligations between stages, carries artifacts forward, and stops the whole composite when a stage does not pass.
additional_fixes.stage_id_normalisation: depends_on writes stage-NN while stage_id writes stage:NN.
